# Provenance: official benchmark evaluators

These files are **vendored from the upstream repository that publishes each benchmark**, so that
Stage-2 evaluation scores each benchmark with its *own* official evaluator — the only scorer
(`accuracy_official`). All adaptation (routing a benchmark to its evaluator, rebuilding the gold answer the way
that evaluator's harness does) lives in `src/official_eval.py`, which *imports* these.

Do not edit these files. If an upstream fix is needed, re-vendor at a new commit and update the
SHA here.

The `mwpbench_util.py` commit is the same SHA that `src/stage2_eval.py` already pins for the

### `_latex2sympy2/` — TheoremQA's LaTeX parser

| Path | Upstream artifact | Version | SHA-256 | License |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `_latex2sympy2/latex2sympy2.py`, `_latex2sympy2/gen/*.py` | PyPI `latex2sympy2-1.9.1-py3-none-any.whl` (https://github.com/OrangeX4/latex2sympy) | 1.9.1 | `44f24d26…a41c601` | MIT (`LICENSE-latex2sympy2.txt`) |
| `_latex2sympy2/antlr4/**` | PyPI `antlr4-python3-runtime-4.7.2.tar.gz`, `src/antlr4/` (https://github.com/antlr/antlr4) | 4.7.2 | `168cdcec…a7193bb50b` | BSD-3-Clause (`LICENSE-antlr4.txt`, from the `4.7.2` tag) |

This tree is **generated**, not hand-copied: `scripts/vendor_latex2sympy2.py` downloads the two
pinned artifacts, refuses on a hash mismatch, and writes the files plus `MANIFEST.json` (full source
hashes and the SHA-256 of every output file). Run it without `--write` to verify the committed tree
against a fresh build; `tests/test_theoremqa_latex2sympy2.py` checks the manifest offline.
`.gitattributes` there disables EOL conversion, because the generated `gen/PS*.py` are CRLF.

Why it is vendored: `latex2sympy2`'s parser was generated by ANTLR 4.7.2 and only loads under the
4.7.2 runtime, but sympy's `parse_latex` (OlympiadBench's judge) needs 4.11, and both runtimes are
the package `antlr4`. The runtime is pure Python, so it is vendored as
`third_party.official_evals._latex2sympy2.antlr4` and latex2sympy2 imports it from there.

## Modifications

The five whole-file entries are **byte-for-byte copies**. The three `(excerpt)` entries copy only
the functions we need, because the upstream modules import a GPU inference stack
(`from vllm import LLM`) or batch/process-pool machinery (`pebble`, `tqdm`) at module scope:

* **`dartmath_extract.py`** — lines 38–215 of upstream `eval.py` (constants, `extract_boxed`,
  `norm_str2bool`, `EvaluatorBase`), i.e. the answer-*extraction* half. A
  `from __future__ import annotations` is prepended so the `RespSampleBase` annotation on the
  unused `EvaluatorBase.eval` stays a lazy string; no runtime behaviour changes. Used by
  OlympiadBench (extraction only — matching is OpenBMB's own judge) and by `dartmath_eval.py`.
* **`dartmath_eval.py`** — lines 288–1399 of the same upstream `eval.py`
  (`latex2sympy_fix` … `EvaluatorMath`), i.e. the *matching* half, which scores `deepmind-math`
  (DART's own DeepMind-Mathematics subset, loaded from the same commit). The excerpt sits between
  BEGIN/END markers, byte-identical (SHA-256 `20022d88…fcf9f12`, checked by
  `tests/test_official_eval.py`). Its import block is upstream lines 1–36 minus exactly the
  batch-only `pebble` / `tqdm` / `.parallel` imports, the annotation-only `.data.RespSampleBase`,
  and `.olympiadbench.OlympiadMathJudger` (construct `EvaluatorMath(use_orig_eq_for_olympiadbench=False)`;
  `eval` only consults that judger for "olympiad*" datasets). All other imports are kept,
  including the sympy names upstream imports "for `eval`", and `from .dartmath_extract import *`
  supplies lines 38–215, so the excerpt runs against upstream's globals. Not excerpted: the batch
  wrappers (`EvaluatorBatchBase`, `EvaluatorMathBatch`) — a process pool with a 5 s timeout per
  call, no scoring logic. Verified: identical verdicts to the unmodified upstream
  `EvaluatorMathBatch.batch_eval` on all 1000 saved generations of each of the four full-FT
  checkpoints.
* **`metamath_extract.py`** — `is_number`, `extract_answer_number` (from `eval_gsm8k.py`) and
  `remove_boxed`, `process_results` (from `eval_math.py`), copied verbatim with two documented
  substitutions: `from fraction import Fraction` → the standard library's `fractions.Fraction`
  (identical parsing for this code path, one less unmaintained dependency), and `util.is_equiv`
  → the vendored Hendrycks `is_equiv`. MetaMath's `util.py` *is* Hendrycks'
  `math_equivalence.py` with the leading underscores stripped from helper names; the bodies,
  including all 19 normalization steps and the `0.5 -> \frac{1}{2}` rule, are identical, so the
  rebinding is semantically a no-op.

* **`_latex2sympy2/`** — import statements only, applied and asserted by the script (counts in
  `MANIFEST.json`): (1) every `from antlr4…` (239 lines, including the 17 the runtime defers into
  function bodies) re-pointed at the private package; (2) latex2sympy2's
  `try: from gen.PS* … except: from .gen.PS*` reduced to the relative branch, so the top-level `gen`
  package that the latex2sympy2 wheel installs can never shadow the vendored parser; (3) the
  runtime's two `from typing.io import TextIO` → `from typing import TextIO` (`typing.io` was removed
  in Python 3.13; on ≤3.12 the two names are the same object, used only as an annotation). Every
  other byte is upstream's. Verified against the real `latex2sympy2==1.9.1` +
  `antlr4-python3-runtime==4.7.2` in a separate environment: identical TheoremQA predictions and
  correctness on all 6,400 saved/fresh generations of the four full-FT checkpoints, and identical
  `latex2sympy` output on 143,490 of 143,491 LaTeX answer strings drawn from every benchmark's
  generations (the other one raises in both, with an exception type that depends on sympy's
  process-global cache — identical when re-run in fresh processes). Compare at a fixed
  `PYTHONHASHSEED`: upstream's `solve()` result ORDER for equations follows Python's
  set-iteration order, so even the real package disagrees with itself across processes there;
  TheoremQA never reaches that path because `answer_clean` splits on `=` first.

`__init__.py` is ours, not upstream. It installs two import shims (a `number_utils` alias, and the
vendored `_latex2sympy2` registered as `latex2sympy2` only while the TheoremQA files import)
precisely so the vendored files need no edits — see its docstring.

## Optional dependency

OlympiadBench and DeepMind-Mathematics need one: sympy's `parse_latex` — called by
`AutoScoringJudge.__init__` and by DART's `EvaluatorMath` — needs
`antlr4-python3-runtime==4.11` (pinned in the top-level `requirements.txt`). Without it `availability()` reports
`unavailable` and the eval refuses to run, never guesses (DART swallows parse errors, so it
would otherwise silently stop matching LaTeX answers). TheoremQA needs nothing.
